TERMINOLOGY · qeva:1:closed-form@2

Closed form

A widely used but non-universal label for formulas considered explicit relative to an allowed vocabulary of operations/functions.

editorialrepresentation · algebra · analysis
Trace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

“Closed form” usually means an explicit formula, but what operations are allowed differs by field and author.

EXACT

The compact statement

QEVA Protocol 0.2 assigns no universal predicate ClosedForm(E). Any claim that an expression is “closed form” must declare the permitted expression language or cite a contextual convention.

Example

a_n=2^n may be called a closed form for the recurrence a_{n+1}=2a_n, a_0=1 when exponentiation is allowed.

Boundary / caveat

Treating “closed form” as one globally defined mathematical property would create false precision.
